headline: Mariana has lost 8% of her body weight (77.9 kg to 71.7 kg) between Sep 5 and Nov 24, 2026, with poor appetite. Her primary caregiver, her son Marcus, also reports exhaustion and is asking for respite.

items.statement: Weight fell at every reading: 77.9 kg (Sep 5), 75.7 kg (Oct 1), 73.6 kg (Oct 28), 71.7 kg (Nov 24). That is 6.2 kg (13.7 lb), or 8.0%, in about 11 weeks.
items.verifier_note: The four weights match the vitals record. The change of 6.2 kg, 13.7 lb and 8.0% matches. Sep 5 to Nov 24 is about 11 weeks.

items.statement: On Nov 24 the dietitian documented poor appetite, skipping breakfast, and eating about 50% of day center lunches. The plan is an oral nutrition supplement twice daily, weekly weights, and a dental check for chewing problems. Follow-through on this plan is not yet documented.
items.verifier_note: The Nov 24 dietitian note matches the statement on appetite, skipped breakfast, 50% of lunches and the plan. No note documents follow-through.

items.statement: On Sep 27 the social worker met with Marcus, her son and primary caregiver. He reported exhaustion and poor sleep, said he is worried about managing evenings alone, and requested respite. Respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed. No outcome is documented.
items.verifier_note: The Sep 27 social work note matches every detail. It documents no outcome.

items.statement: PCP progress notes on Sep 2, Sep 27, and Nov 27 each say chronic conditions are stable with no plan change. The Nov 27 note, three days after the dietitian's weight loss assessment, does not mention the weight loss. Blood pressures (130/74, 134/77, 130/72) were below the 140/90 threshold. There were no encounters and no medication changes in the period.
items.verifier_note: All three PCP notes say conditions are stable and the plan continues. The Nov 27 note does not mention weight loss and falls 3 days after Nov 24. The BP readings are all below 140/90. The encounters record is empty and no medications were started or stopped.

items.statement: Day center attendance on Oct 9 included chair exercise and music group, with most of lunch eaten. She enjoyed the gardening group on Oct 4, and home care aides noted she was in good spirits on Sep 21 and Oct 26. Intake at lunch has since dropped to about 50% (Nov 24).
items.verifier_note: Each note matches: Oct 9 day center, Oct 4 gardening, aide notes on Sep 21 and Oct 26, and the Nov 24 intake of about 50%.

questions_for_team: Who is confirming that the twice-daily supplement, weekly weights, and dental referral have started, and when will the next weight be reviewed?
Does the PCP know about the 8% weight loss, and should the team look for causes beyond poor appetite and chewing problems?
What respite and evening support can be offered to Marcus, and has he followed up since Sep 27?
Could the low breakfast and lunch intake be connected to the caregiver's strain or evening and morning routines at home?

Two withheld notes (08e17e4e-n013 and 08e17e4e-n014) dispute the Nov 24 weight loss assessment without any new measurement. The team should review them and decide how to verify the Nov 24 entry. The vitals record shows the same downward weight trend.

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters in it: ED visits, urgent care, hospital admissions, observation stays, and any readmissions.
Falls and near-falls: count and document any falls or near-falls in the window, injury severity, and whether a post-fall assessment was done. Note osteoporosis history given fracture risk.
Cardiac review (ischemic heart disease, hypertension, metoprolol, nitroglycerin): chest pain episodes, nitroglycerin use frequency, dyspnea, edema, and any cardiology visits or ECG/echo results.

Blood pressure trend: review all readings in the window for hypotension or hypertension, orthostatic readings if recorded, and dizziness reports, since she takes metoprolol and has a hypertension history.
Heart rate trend on metoprolol: flag low resting heart rate, syncope, or fatigue reports.

Diabetes and glycemia (type 2 diabetes, prediabetes, hyperglycemia, metabolic syndrome): review glucose and HbA1c results, any hypoglycemia events, and whether any diabetes medication changes occurred. Note that no diabetes-specific medication appears on the active list; confirm whether this reflects diet control or a reconciliation gap.

Kidney function (CKD stage 1 due to diabetes): review the most recent creatinine, eGFR, and urine albumin-to-creatinine results and their trend against prior values. Check that the statin and other meds were reviewed against current renal function.
Lipids (hypertriglyceridemia, on simvastatin 20 mg since 1995): review the most recent lipid panel and any statin dose or agent changes; confirm adherence and whether any lipid targets are overdue.
Anemia and B12 (on vitamin B12 injections since 1970): confirm injection schedule adherence and dates given in the window, review hemoglobin/CBC trend, and check for any missed or overdue B12 doses.

Weight and BMI (obesity, BMI 30+): review weight trend across the window, flag change of more than 5% or unintended loss, and note any nutrition referral status. Also check for mobility or appetite changes affecting intake.

Medication reconciliation: compare active list to dispensing and pharmacy records for starts and stops in the window, check for duplicate or interacting agents, and confirm no allergies are documented, since the allergy list is empty and should be verified with the participant.
Function and ADLs/IADLs: compare current ADL and IADL status against the last review, including mobility aids, transfers, bathing, medication management, and meal preparation. Flag any decline.
Cognition and mood: review any cognitive screen results, delirium or confusion episodes, and depression screen scores, plus any new mood or sleep concerns recorded in the window.
Attendance and engagement: check PACE center attendance, missed days, transportation issues, and participation in therapies, meals, or social programs during the window.
Caregiver and social situation: confirm current living situation, caregiver availability or changes, support needs, and any safety concerns noted since the last review.

Care-plan items due: list care-plan goals and assessments with due dates falling in or before 2026-11-30 (for example kidney labs, lipid panel, HbA1c, eye and foot exams, bone density follow-up, and B12 schedule), and mark which are completed, overdue, or need scheduling.
Summarize for the IDT: list the changes found in the window with source dates, flag items needing team discussion, and avoid treatment recommendations, leaving decisions to the clinicians.
